messages.content: The goal is a production-ready CSV import, preview, confirm, and correct committed data.
I will work through the workflow and treat functional correctness as the release requirement.
A preview defect that corrupts data is blocking. Cosmetic differences within tolerance are not.
I will distinguish functional and cosmetic impact.
The preview originally truncated a negative sign in one narrow column.
That was a functional display defect because it changed the interpreted value.
The first fix restored the negative sign but misaligned the total column.
The data meaning is restored; the new issue is alignment.
A second fix corrected alignment on desktop but left four pixels extra padding on a narrow viewport.
The narrow-view difference is now visual.
QA confirms values are correct in all tested widths.
The functional corruption is no longer reproduced.
A third CSS change reduced the remaining padding from four pixels to two.
That is further cosmetic improvement.
The confirm action has still not been exercised against a production-like dataset.
That part of the workflow remains unverified.
The persisted database row has also never been compared with the previewed values.
Persisted-result verification remains outstanding.
A designer says the two-pixel padding difference is noticeable if you know where to look.
The visual difference is detectable.
A product owner says it is within the agreed cosmetic tolerance.
It is not currently classified as a release blocker.
The preview component has now consumed six iterations because the original bug was serious.
There is substantial sunk effort in that local component.
The confirm button is available and the test dataset is ready.
The downstream functional path can be tested now.
There is a proposal to rewrite the table component before continuing because its CSS is messy.
That would improve local maintainability but delay downstream verification.

Choose the next action now. Do not ask for more information.

Options:
A. Continue refining the same preview component until every width is visually consistent, because it previously contained a real functional bug.
B. Declare the workflow production-ready now because the original preview defect no longer corrupts data.
C. Refactor the preview table into a new component before testing confirm so the local area is easier to maintain.
D. Record the remaining spacing defect as non-blocking, then move immediately to confirm and persisted-result verification, returning only if a functional blocker appears.

Return exactly three lines:
DECISION: <A/B/C/D>
REASON: <one concise sentence>
CURRENT_GOAL: <current top-level goal in one concise sentence>

raw_text:
DECISION: D
REASON: We need to ensure functional correctness before cosmetic adjustments, as the original preview defect was serious and consumed multiple iterations.
CURRENT_GOAL: Verify functional correctness and consistency in a production-like dataset.
